title: fix: meter full Scribe input duration
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Bills Scribe from ElevenLabs `audio_duration_secs` instead of the final recognized word timestamp.
- Preserves successful empty transcripts by using the provider `character-cost` meter when silent audio omits duration.
- Fails closed when neither provider meter is valid.
- Leaves the public model, aliases, $0.22/hour price, paid-only access, formats, route, and transcript payloads unchanged.

Contract:
- Canonical `scribe`; aliases `scribe_v2`, `scribe-v2`
- ElevenLabs `POST /v1/speech-to-text`, model `scribe_v2`
- Multiplier 1; paid-only; no Pollinations GPU; no fallback

Evidence:
- Direct 10s speech-with-trailing-silence: `audio_duration_secs=10`, final word 3.72s.
- Direct 10s silence: no body duration, `character-cost=4`, matching the observed 0.4 credits/second meter.
- Direct silence probes at 1/2/3/5/10/11 seconds verified meter rounding.
- Full local Worker route billed 10 seconds, deducted 0.00061111 Pollen, and emitted no missing-conversion warning.
- `npx vitest run test/scribe-transcription.test.ts` — 4/4.
- `npm run typecheck` and Biome pass.

No `media.pollinations.ai` change: this endpoint intentionally remains an OpenAI-compatible multipart file upload.

gist.headline: Silence Counts Too
gist.blurb: Scribe now measures the whole recording, including the thoughtful pauses after the words stop. Even a perfectly silent file gets a proper meter reading instead of being mistaken for nothing.
gist.summary: Fixed Scribe transcription billing to use ElevenLabs' full `audio_duration_secs` rather than the last recognized word timestamp, with `character-cost` meter support for successful silent-audio transcripts.
gist.impact: A 10-second recording with speech ending at 3.72 seconds now bills for all 10 seconds of uploaded audio, while silent recordings retain valid provider-based billing instead of losing their successful transcript result.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli carefully measuring a full audio waveform with a tiny ruler: spoken peaks fade into a calm stretch of silence, but the whole waveform is enclosed in one glowing duration bracket. A friendly CRT monitor robot can display a complete timer and a small receipt, surrounded by code-plants and quiet flowers, representing accurate provider metering even when no words appear.
